chapter: New York 1936-39 (second pass of the transcript)
title: Billy Hicks and his Sizzling Six (second pass)
summary: Repeat account of the Savoy engagement, the sidemen and the repertoire, with the pianists of the day.

bands.name: Billy Hicks and His Sizzling Six

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Paying me back. And, I started at the Savoy Ballroom, Billy Hicks got the gig at the Savoy Ballroom opposite Chick Webb. And we stayed a year and a half.
Now, I don't know too much about that band, I mean, I've known the name, it's such a catchy name, Billy Hicks and his Sizzling Six.
But, tell me something about that
Well, we had Edmund , Fernando Arbello, Skippy Boland, Arnold Boland, Cyril Hanes, we had a jumping band.
It was an arranged sort of thing, you know.
Did Edmund double on anything or just -
No, he just played clarinet. It was my first meeting, he had just left Claude Hopkins band and we were there a year and a half. And it was the year that I joined the Union.
Oh, he was a trumpet player.
He was -- he didn't go too high and he didn't go too low. He was right in the middle, but he was fantastic. But then we had to wear funny hats and all.
What kind of a book did you have, as you said, it wasn't Dixieland.
Yeah, we played the popular songs of the day but they were more or less arranged and we rehearsed them.
And Cyril Hanes was on piano?

Cyril Hanes was the follow-up pianist for -- was a real nut, can't think of his name. Cyril followed him and then when the Savoy Sultans followed us, Cyril was with them, because he was the favorite pianist at that point. Ram (phonetic) was a famous pianist at that point.
Yes. And Eddie Heywood and Teddy Wilson, they were the favorite pianists. Edgar Hayes.
But, Clyde Hart, Billy Cowl hadn't come to New York.
